reviewer: R3 - diagnostic logic: fold and drag-line rules, grain and balance, symptom-to-cause relationships
scope_and_method: SCOPE. CC-02, CC-17, CC-22, CC-23, CC-24, CC-26 and CC-29 checked against sources as briefed; CC-20 and CC-25 added because the sign data contradicts them. All 43 fit signs and all 129 candidate causes read in full and analysed for internal consistency. Twelve signs additionally web-verified. SOURCES. All FOUR documents the taxonomy cites were obtained and read end to end: Texas AgriLife E-372 (S-0003), NMSU C-228 (S-0001), NMSU C-227 (S-0002) and WSU EM4582 (S-0004). A CORRECTION I MADE TO MYSELF, recorded because it changed a headline finding: I first reported EM4582 as unobtainable after a failed retrieval, and that was wrong. The URL in the project's own source record returns HTTP 200 and a 123 KB PDF; I have read it. The finding that replaced it is worse for the book, not better - the document is real and checkable, and it does not contain CC-22, CC-24 or CC-29. TWO OBSERVATIONS ABOUT THE SOURCE SET AS A WHOLE. First, NMSU C-228, which is attached as a source_ref to 34 of the 43 signs, contains no diagnostic content at all - it is a catalogue of alteration recipes with no discussion of wrinkles, folds, drag lines, observation order or symptom-to-cause reasoning. It supports the REMEDIES the taxonomy names, and supports them well, but it cannot support a single one of the 129 discriminating-evidence claims. Second, the one document that would have supported them is one the project does not cite: WSU E.M. 2246 'Garment Fitting' (Hazel L. Roberts, December 1962), from the same publisher as S-0004, reachable, and organised exactly as this book is - sign, then cause, then remedy. Several of my findings come from it. READING THIS FILE. Some claim_id values appear more than once; each occurrence is a different finding about the same record (for example SYM-023.C1 appears once for its confirming_measurement and once for its distinguishing_evidence). Findings whose source_quality is 'internal_logic' are the evidence collisions from task 4(a) and carry no external citation by design: they show that the stated evidence cannot do the job the schema requires of it, which is a matter of logic, not of sources. The same 28 collisions are also listed in full under the top-level key 'evidence_collisions'.

twelve_web_verified_signs.why_these_twelve: Chosen on three criteria: (a) the sign carries one of the four core rules, so an error propagates to every other record - SYM-009 is the paradigm case of CC-22 (horizontal fold = excess length), SYM-016 and SYM-004 are the paradigm cases of CC-24 (drag lines point at their source), SYM-027 and SYM-035 are the records where the horizontal-fold class is applied to a shortage, SYM-040 is CC-29 in data form; (b) the sign is the book's own most-frequent or highest-consequence claim - SYM-016 is labelled 'the sign the target reader meets most often', SYM-021 puts a full bust adjustment and moving a button on the same evidence, SYM-001 is where the book says diagnosis is most often missed; (c) the record looked internally unsound before any searching - SYM-013's observation combines two opposite armhole faults, SYM-023 and SYM-036 rest on measurements that are not independent, SYM-033 attributes a bilateral twist to a unilateral construction error. Together they cover both garment halves, all three directional sign classes, and every one of the seven conceptual claims I was asked to attack.
twelve_web_verified_signs.outcome_summary: Every one of the twelve required a revision. SYM-023 was the closest to sound - its three evidence fields are genuinely mutually exclusive - but the literature supplies a cause it omits (flat derriere) whose fabric signature is identical to its C1, and a precondition it treats as a sibling (hip width). SYM-009 and SYM-016 survive as claims but rest on colliding evidence. SYM-001, SYM-004, SYM-013, SYM-027, SYM-035, SYM-036 and SYM-040 each carry a substantive error: an inverted symmetry criterion; an observation that is the literature's SLOPING-shoulder sign with a square-shoulder cause filed under it, plus a localisation rule the record's own data contradicts; an observation combining two opposite armhole faults; a sign_class that inverts the book's own core rule; a physical test an extension service states cannot discriminate; a distinguishing_evidence field describing a state its own measurements cannot report; and a candidate-cause list missing the whole fabric-and-cut family. SYM-021 and SYM-033 carry collisions with concrete, avoidable costs. The one structural pattern worth naming: nine of the twelve fail not because the CAUSE is wrong but because the EVIDENCE offered to distinguish it is a restatement of the observation, a measurement the two causes share, or a test that relieves both.
